Support for integration paths involving externally maintained components where shared hardware-wallet flows intersect
Vendor-required product or security audits where firmware or app changes trigger them
request.recipient: Intersect 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Hardware Wallet Maintenance 2026 for 12 months of production maintenance of Cardano hardware-wallet support.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,310,960 ada, consisting of 1,272,777 ada for Cardano Hardware Wallet Maintenance & Compatibility Assurance and 38,183 ada for an Intersect Budget Administration fee.

The work is scoped to continuity maintenance rather than building a new wallet product, covering compatibility, security, supporting libraries/tooling, release support, and vendor-required audit work.
The proposer states that continuous hardware-wallet maintenance is needed because Cardano, Ledger, or Trezor changes can otherwise break secure access for users and integrations.

The proposer states that the project aligns with Cardano strategic Pillar 1 for secure, reliable, interoperable signing and secondarily with Pillar 2 for secure UX, developer experience, and adoption.

The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The proposer states that the requested amount does not, at submission, breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
Prior related treasury and Catalyst funding is disclosed through several governance-action and Project Catalyst links.
Intersect will administer funds using a 2026 instance of the Sundae Labs treasury management smart contract framework with TRSC and PSSC addresses listed in the document.

The proposed smart-contract administration includes five Intersect admin roles, three Intersect leadership roles, and an Oversight Committee of six named external entities for checks and balances on specified actions.
A public dashboard and on-chain records are identified as mechanisms for community audit and tracking of the withdrawn ada.

summary: The document describes a 1,310,960 ada treasury withdrawal submitted by Intersect for 2026 hardware-wallet maintenance, with budget breakdown, scope, governance-process references, NCL assertion, prior-funding disclosures, and smart-contract fund administration details.
